title: What If Gravity Vanished for 5 Seconds?
caption: Five seconds without gravity. Would Earth survive?
script: [A crowded city street suddenly lifting into the air] What if gravity vanished for just five seconds? [People and cars floating upward in a cinematic wide shot] Everything not tied down would begin to drift away from the ground. [A train lifting from the tracks as passengers grab their seats] Trains, cars, even ocean water could rise. [Gravity snaps back as objects slam down] Then gravity returns. And the real disaster starts when everything falls back at once. [Aerial view of floating debris above skyscrapers] At first it might look like a dream, until you realize there is nowhere safe to land.

title: What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn?
caption: Imagine looking up and seeing gigantic rings across the sky.
script: [A photorealistic sunrise over a city with immense rings overhead] What if Earth had rings like Saturn? [Camera moves through glittering ice and rock orbiting Earth] Our skies would look spectacular. [A city at night beneath a bright silver arc] Some places might never get completely dark because sunlight would reflect off the rings. [Aerial view of deep shadows sweeping a continent] But those rings could also cast enormous shadows across Earth. Beautiful from the ground. Complicated for life underneath. [A child points at bands crossing the blue afternoon sky] Their brightness would change with the seasons and where you lived. Astronomers would have a whole new sky to study.
thumbnailPrompt: Photorealistic cinematic vertical thumbnail. Earthlike city skyline beneath huge luminous rings spanning the sky, a human silhouette looking upward, golden sunset against an enormous silver ring. One clear visual idea, high contrast, beautiful and mysterious. No words, logos or watermarks.

title: What If the Sun Went Dark for One Hour?
caption: The Sun disappears for one hour. What happens next?
script: [A busy seaside city in sunlight abruptly fades to darkness] What if the Sun went dark for just one hour? [Streetlights switch on beneath a black daytime sky] About eight minutes later, daylight would suddenly vanish. [A family on a balcony looking toward the stars] The stars would appear where the blue sky had been. [Aerial view of Earth at night, then sunlight slowly returning] Earth would not freeze instantly. But the sudden darkness would shock people and wildlife everywhere. Then, just as strangely, day would return. [Birds settle into trees while confused commuters turn on phone flashlights] Animals could behave as if night had arrived. Scientists would race to understand what had happened.

Half a modern city in sunshine, the other half under impossibly star-filled black daytime sky, startled people in foreground, bold light-dark split. title: What If the Moon Moved Twice as Close?
caption: A giant Moon sounds beautiful. The tides tell another story.
script: [An enormous photorealistic full Moon rises above a harbor] What if the Moon suddenly moved twice as close to Earth? [People on a beach stare at the giant moon] It would dominate the night sky. [Ocean water surges into a seaside street] But the strongest change would be in our oceans. The Moon's tide-raising pull would become dramatically stronger. [Satellite view of vast coastal regions at night] Coastal communities could face extreme tides. A spectacular view in the sky could come with a dangerous cost below. [Fishermen struggle to secure boats at a flooded pier] Night skies might be brighter, but the changing tides would matter far more to anyone who lives near the coast.

title: What If Every Satellite Stopped Working?
caption: One moment, every satellite goes silent. Then what?
script: [A space station camera view of hundreds of satellites around Earth] What if every satellite suddenly stopped working? [A driver watches a GPS map freeze on the dashboard] Navigation could fail across huge areas. [Cargo ships in a busy harbor switch to paper charts] Weather forecasts would lose vital observations. [Television broadcasts flicker and an aircraft flies overhead] Some communications would be disrupted too. [A stunning orbital view of Earth, now surrounded by dark satellites] Life would continue, but much of the invisible technology we depend on would suddenly be missing. [A weather forecaster points to missing satellite images on a studio screen] Emergency teams would fall back on ground-based systems and older methods. Not everything would fail, but coordination would become harder.

title: What If the Oceans Froze Overnight?
caption: Imagine every ocean turning to ice in a single night.
script: [Ocean waves abruptly turning to solid ice below a cliff] What if every ocean froze overnight? [A cargo ship trapped between jagged ice sheets] Shipping routes could close instantly. [Seabirds circling above a frozen sea] Marine food webs would face catastrophe as their habitats changed. [A storm cloud moves above the white frozen ocean] The oceans normally store and move enormous amounts of heat. [Orbital view of a pale frozen planet] Turning them to ice would transform weather and climate worldwide. This would be far more than a cold winter. [Whales swim beneath thick new ice while the surface glows white] The greatest disruption would not be the frozen surface alone. It would be the immense change to the planet's delicate balance.
